academic_translation: Subhūti replied, "Blessed One, it is so.
translation: Subhuti answered, "Blessed One, it is so."

academic_translation: That collection of subtle particles would be numerous.
translation: That bunch of tiny specks would be very large.

academic_translation: Why is that? Because, Blessed One, if a collection of subtle particles existed, the Blessed One would not have spoken of a 'collection of subtle particles'.
translation: Why is that? Because, Blessed One, if a bunch of tiny specks really existed, the Blessed One would not have talked about a 'bunch of tiny specks'.

academic_translation: Why is that? It is because what the Blessed One has spoken of as a 'collection of subtle particles', the Tathāgata has spoken of as no collection.
translation: Why is that? Because what the Blessed One called a 'bunch of tiny specks', the Thus-Gone One said is not a bunch.

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called a 'collection of subtle particles.'
translation: That is why it is called a 'bunch of tiny specks'.

academic_translation: What the Tathāgata has spoken of as a 'three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system,' the Tathāgata has spoken of as not being a system;
translation: What the Thus-Gone One called a 'universe of a billion worlds', the Thus-Gone One said is not a world realm.

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called a 'three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system.'
translation: That is why that world realm is called a 'universe of a billion worlds'.

academic_translation: Why is that? Blessed One, because if a world system existed, that itself would be grasping at a totality.
translation: Why is that? Blessed One, because if a world realm existed, that would be clinging to a lump.

academic_translation: Because what the Tathāgata has spoken of as grasping at a totality, the Tathāgata has spoken of as no grasping,
translation: Because what the Thus-Gone One called clinging to a lump, the Thus-Gone One said is no clinging.

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called "grasping at a totality."
translation: That is why it is called "clinging to a lump."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, grasping at a totality is itself a conventional designation;
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, clinging to a lump is just an everyday name.

academic_translation: that phenomenon is inexpressible, yet it is grasped by childish ordinary beings.
translation: That thing cannot be put into words, but naive ordinary beings grasp at it."

academic_translation: Subhūti, if someone were to say: The Tathāgata has spoken of a view of a self,
translation: "Subhuti, if someone said, 'The Thus-Gone One spoke of a view of a self,'"

academic_translation: If someone were to say, "The Tathāgata has spoken of the view of a sentient being, the view of a life-force, and the view of a person," would they be speaking correctly?
translation: "If someone said, 'The Thus-Gone One spoke of the view of a living being, the view of a life, and the view of a person,' would they be right?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied, Blessed One, it is not so.
translation: Subhuti replied, "Blessed One, it is not so."

academic_translation: Sugata, it is not so.
translation: "Well-Gone One, it is not so."

academic_translation: Why is that? Because, Blessed One, what the Tathāgata has spoken of as the view of a self, the Tathāgata has spoken of as no view.
translation: "Why is that? Because, Blessed One, what the Thus-Gone One spoke of as the view of a self, the Thus-Gone One spoke of as no view."

academic_translation: Therefore, it is called the view of a self.
translation: "That is why it is called the view of a self."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said, Subhūti, in this regard, one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should know, see, and resolve upon all phenomena in this way:
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, anyone who has truly entered the awakening hero's vehicle should know, see, and understand all things in this way:"

academic_translation: They should be known in such a way that one does not abide in the perception of a phenomenon.
translation: They should be known without holding onto the idea of a thing.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'perception of a phenomenon, perception of a phenomenon,' the Tathāgata has spoken of it as no perception.
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, as for what is called 'idea of a thing, idea of a thing,' the Thus-Gone One has said it is no idea.

academic_translation: Therefore it is called 'perception of a phenomenon, perception of a phenomenon'.
translation: That is why it is called 'idea of a thing, idea of a thing'.

academic_translation: Furthermore, Subhūti, compared to a bodhisattva great being who fills immeasurable and incalculable world systems with the seven precious substances and gives them as a gift, if a son of noble family or daughter of noble family writes down, takes up, bears, reads, masters, or extensively and perfectly teaches to others even just a four-line verse from this perfection of wisdom, they will produce much more merit, incalculable and immeasurable, on that basis.
translation: Furthermore, Subhuti, think of a great awakening hero who fills countless world realms with the seven precious things and gives them all away as a gift. Now think of a son of a good family or a daughter of a good family. They might write down, learn, keep, read, understand, or fully teach others even just a four-line verse from this perfection, perfect wisdom. This person will create much more stored-up goodness. It will be too great to count or measure.

academic_translation: How does one perfectly teach it? Just as one does not perfectly teach it, in that way one perfectly teaches it.
translation: How do you perfectly teach it? Just as you do not perfectly teach it, that is how you perfectly teach it.

academic_translation: Therefore it is called perfectly teaching.
translation: That is why it is called perfectly teaching.

academic_translation: Like a star, a visual aberration, a lamp, an illusion, a dewdrop, a bubble, a dream, lightning, and a cloud—thus should one view all conditioned phenomena.
translation: See everything that is put together like this: like a star, blurred sight, a lamp, an illusion, a dewdrop, a bubble, a dream, lightning, and a cloud.

tibetan: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས་དེ་སྐད་ཅེས་བཀའ་སྩལ་ནས། གནས་བརྟན་རབ་འབྱོར་དང༌། དགེ་སློང་དེ་དག་དང༌། བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་དག་དང༌། འཁོར་བཞི་པོ་དགེ་སློང་དང༌། དགེ་སློང་མ་དང༌། དགེ་བསྙེན་དང༌། དགེ་བསྙེན་མ་དང༌། ལྷ་དང༌། མི་དང་ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་དང༌། དྲི་ཟར་བཅས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཡི་རངས་ཏེ།
academic_translation: After the Blessed One had spoken thus, the elder Subhūti, those monks, those bodhisattvas, and the fourfold assembly of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, along with the world with its gods, humans, demigods, and gandharvas, rejoiced,
translation: After the Blessed One said this, everyone rejoiced. The elder Subhuti, the monks, and the awakening heroes were full of joy. The four groups of followers—the monks, nuns, lay followers, and laywomen—were very happy. The whole world rejoiced, along with its gods, humans, jealous gods, and scent-eaters.

academic_translation: and highly praised what the Blessed One had spoken.
translation: They greatly praised what the Blessed One had said.

academic_translation: The noble Mahāyāna sūtra entitled the Diamond Cutter perfection of wisdom is complete.

locked_terms.use: Perfect Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond

translation: The noble Great Vehicle sacred text called Perfect Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond is complete. This is the Diamond Cutter perfection of perfect wisdom.

academic_translation: namo bhagavate prajñāpāramitāye oṃ natadatita iliśi iliśi miliśi miliśi bhinayan bhinayan namo bhagavate pratyaṃprate iriti iriti mirati miriti śuriti śuriti uśuri uśuri bhuyuye bhuyuye svāhā
translation: A sacred chant.

academic_translation: By reciting this essence of the Diamond Cutter once, it becomes equal to reading the Diamond Cutter ninety million times.
translation: Saying this core, the heart of the Diamond Cutter, just once is the same as reading the Diamond Cutter ninety million times.

academic_translation: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetun teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat, teṣāñca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mihāśramaṇaye svāhā
translation: A sacred chant.
